entries.name: AgentRes Restaurant Booking
entries.description: Search restaurants and create/manage table reservations programmatically. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: POST https://agentres.dev/api/book with JSON body {venue_id, config_id, party_size, day} — config_id must first be obtained from GET https://agentres.dev/api/availability
usage.outputShape: body.success (bool), body.kind ("booked"), body.resy_token, body.reservation_id
quirks: RESY-OTP-CONFIRMED 2026-06-09: a booking call sent a real Resy OTP email to the user — the endpoint is LIVE and initiates Resy verification; completing a reservation requires the OTP, so it is needs-input (not broken).
DID NOT PAY — not testable in an automated QA run.

Required field config_id is an opaque dynamic 'slot config token' that must be fetched live from GET /api/availability?venue_id=&party_size=&day= for a real venue with an open slot on a FUTURE date; it cannot be fabricated. The schema example (venue_id 6194, day 2026-05-01) is a stale placeholder.
Two-step flow: (1) GET /api/availability to get slots[].config_id, then (2) POST /api/book. /api/availability is itself x402-gated (returns 402 with amount 0).

authMode=apiKey+paid. The decoded x402 resource description says it books 'for the authenticated user' — requires a Resy account auth/API key context, which is not provided. Booking destination is the authenticated user's Resy account, not a settable recipient.
OUTWARD/IRREVERSIBLE: creates a real Resy restaurant reservation. Requires human approval and a real authenticated Resy user before calling.
Payment network is Base USDC (eip155:8453, $0.010); the 402 also advertises a Tempo charge method in www-authenticate.

APPROVAL-GATED: this is an OUTWARD/irreversible action (real charge / order / shipment). Shape is from the provider OpenAPI/discovery and was NOT QA-executed (we do not place real bookings/purchases as tests). The needsApproval gate fires before any real execution.
DEAD 2026-06-11: Requires a linked Resy account + credit card + OTP completion — not usable via x402 alone. De-scoped (ash 2026-06-11).
usage.guide: Booking is a two-step flow and creates a real Resy reservation, so confirm with the user first. First call GET https://agentres.dev/api/availability?venue_id=<resy_id>&party_size=<n>&day=<YYYY-MM-DD> (x402-gated) to get slots[].config_id for an open slot on a future date. Then POST https://agentres.dev/api/book with JSON {venue_id, config_id, party_size, day} using that config_id. The endpoint books for the authenticated Resy user, so a Resy account auth/API key context is required (authMode=apiKey+paid) — you cannot set an arbitrary recipient. On success read body.success, body.reservation_id, and body.resy_token.

entries.name: Agent Restaurant Reservation
entries.description: Restaurant reservation API for AI agents — check availability and book tables. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: POST https://agentres.dev/api/book with JSON body {venue_id, config_id, party_size, day} and content-type: application/json. x402 wallet auth on Base (USDC) — booking costs 0.01 USDC; all setup/search/availability endpoints are $0 (wallet signs for identity only). (Registry alias url agentic-reservations.vercel.app also works.)
usage.outputShape: body.success (bool), body.resy_token, body.reservation_id, body.kind
quirks: RESY-OTP-CONFIRMED 2026-06-09: a booking call sent a real Resy OTP email to the user — the endpoint is LIVE and initiates Resy verification; completing a reservation requires the OTP, so it is needs-input (not broken).

NOT a single-call endpoint: /api/book is the terminal step of a multi-step session flow. Prereqs that cannot be invented: a real venue_id (from GET /api/search?query=&city=), and an ephemeral config_id slot token (from GET /api/availability?venue_id=&party_size=&day=). Docs: 'Config IDs expire — always fetch fresh availability before booking.'

A LINKED Resy account is mandatory: GET /api/me must return resy_linked:true. Linking is a two-step OTP flow on POST /api/link-resy: step1 {em_address} sends a 6-digit code to the user's real Resy.com email, step2 {em_address, code} completes it. Field is em_address (NOT email). Without a linked Resy account /api/book returns 400 NO_LINKED_ACCOUNT and the 0.01 USDC is lost.
First-time wallet must POST /api/account {email} (after GET /api/me returns 401) before link-resy. $0 identity call.

REAL-WORLD IRREVERSIBLE ACTION: books an actual restaurant table on the user's Resy account. Provider warns automated bookings may get the Resy account suspended/banned. Requires explicit human 'yes' confirmation before calling (docs make this a hard rule). Use POST /api/cancel (after GET /api/reservations to get resy_token) to undo.

Base domain is agentres.dev; full schema at /openapi.json, agent guide at /skill.md. Only /api/book is paid (0.01 USDC); /api/me, /api/account, /api/link-resy, /api/search, /api/availability, /api/reservations, /api/cancel are all $0 identity-only.
Errors include retryable + next_step fields; 409 ALREADY_BOOKED = user already has a reservation there; 502 BOOKING_FAILED = upstream Resy failure.

APPROVAL-GATED: this is an OUTWARD/irreversible action (real charge / order / shipment). Shape is from the provider OpenAPI/discovery and was NOT QA-executed (we do not place real bookings/purchases as tests). The needsApproval gate fires before any real execution.

DEAD 2026-06-11: Resy-based: needs a linked Resy account + card + a real OTP relay to complete; /book is the terminal step of a multi-step Resy session. Not usable via x402 alone. De-scoped (ash 2026-06-11).
usage.guide: This is a multi-step Resy booking flow, not a one-shot call — do NOT POST /api/book directly. First GET /api/me to check resy_linked; if false, run the one-time setup: POST /api/account {email} then the two-step OTP on POST /api/link-resy ({em_address} to send a code, then {em_address, code} — needs the user's real Resy.com email and the 6-digit code they receive). Then GET /api/search to get a venue_id, GET /api/availability to get a FRESH config_id (they expire), present a full summary and get explicit user 'yes', then POST /api/book {venue_id, config_id, party_size, day}. Read body.success / body.reservation_id / body.resy_token. Booking costs 0.01 USDC via x402 on Base; everything else is free. This books a real table and can get the Resy account banned — always confirm with the user first.

entries.name: StableTravel Hotel List by City
entries.description: List hotels in a city by IATA city code (Amadeus reference data). Returns hotelId values used to fetch offers. This is the discovery step; it does NOT return prices/offers.

usage.callShape: GET https://stabletravel.dev/api/hotels/list?cityCode=PAR&max=5
usage.outputShape: data[].{hotelId,name,chainCode,iataCode,dupeId,geoCode.{latitude,longitude},address.{countryCode,postalCode,cityName,lines[]},lastUpdate}; meta.count
quirks: cityCode is REQUIRED and must be a 3-letter IATA CITY code (PAR, LON, NYC) — not a hotel name or country.
Returns hotel directory entries only (no prices). Feed hotelId into /api/hotels/search to get bookable offers.
Optional filters: radius, radiusUnit(KM|MILE), chainCodes, amenities, ratings(1-5 csv), hotelScore(BEDBANK|DIRECTCHAIN|ALL), max(default 100).
402 pre-flight body is empty; pay and you get 200 JSON.
meta.count is the total catalog size (e.g. 1694 for PAR), not the number of rows returned.

entries.name: StableTravel Hotel Offers Search
entries.description: Search bookable hotel offers (prices, rooms, cancellation policy) for one or more Amadeus hotel IDs and a date range. Returns offer.id values needed for booking.

usage.callShape: GET https://stabletravel.dev/api/hotels/search?hotelIds=HLPAR266,MDPARMER&adults=1&checkInDate=2026-08-15&checkOutDate=2026-08-16
usage.outputShape: data[].{type:'hotel-offers',hotel.{hotelId,name,chainCode,cityCode,latitude,longitude},available,offers[].{id,checkInDate,checkOutDate,rateCode,room.{type,typeEstimated,description.text},price.{currency,base,total,taxes[]},policies.{cancellations[],deposit,refundable.cancellationRefund},self},self}
quirks: hotelIds is REQUIRED — COMMA-SEPARATED Amadeus hotelId codes (e.g. HLPAR266). Get these from /api/hotels/list or /api/hotels/list/by-geocode first.
checkInDate/checkOutDate must be FUTURE dates (YYYY-MM-DD); past/today dates yield no offers.
offers[].id is the offerId used by /api/hotels/offer and /api/hotels/book — capture it.
Prices come back in the hotel's native currency (e.g. EUR) unless currencyCode is passed (enum of ~33 codes incl USD,EUR,GBP).

Optional filters: adults(default 1), priceRange(e.g. 100-300), currencyCode, paymentPolicy(GUARANTEE|DEPOSIT|NONE), boardType(ROOM_ONLY|BREAKFAST|HALF_BOARD|FULL_BOARD|ALL_INCLUSIVE), includeClosed, bestRateOnly, lang.
available:false hotels are omitted/marked; not every hotelId returns offers for a given date.

entries.name: StableTravel Hotel Autocomplete
entries.description: Autocomplete hotel names by keyword; returns matching hotels with their Amadeus hotelIds, city/country, and geocode. Cheap name-to-hotelId resolver.

usage.callShape: GET https://stabletravel.dev/api/hotels/autocomplete?keyword=PARIS&subType=HOTEL_GDS&max=5
usage.outputShape: data[].{id,name,iataCode,subType,relevance,type:'location',hotelIds[],address.{cityName,countryCode},geoCode.{latitude,longitude}}
quirks: BOTH keyword AND subType are REQUIRED. subType enum is HOTEL_LEISURE or HOTEL_GDS.
GOTCHA (observed): subType=HOTEL_LEISURE returned HTTP 500 'Amadeus API error: Unknown error' even for a valid keyword; subType=HOTEL_GDS succeeded. Prefer HOTEL_GDS.
Returns hotelIds[] per match (note: array) — use those with /api/hotels/search.
Cheapest hotel endpoint ($0.0054). Optional: countryCode, lang, max.
Upstream Amadeus errors surface as {success:false,error} with a non-2xx status — treat 5xx as retry-with-HOTEL_GDS or transient.

entries.name: StableTravel Hotel Booking
entries.description: Create a real hotel booking order against an offer (Amadeus hotel-order). OUTWARD/irreversible: provisions an actual reservation. Not auto-called.

usage.callShape: POST https://stabletravel.dev/api/hotels/book  body: {data:{type:'hotel-order',guests[],travelAgent,roomAssociations[],payment}}

guests[].tid is a numeric guest index referenced by roomAssociations; do not confuse with a string id.
Real booking needs a fresh offerId (from /api/hotels/offer) tied to roomAssociations[].hotelOfferId, plus a real payment.paymentCard. Offer must still be live or Amadeus rejects.
Cheapest write endpoint ($0.00216) but the x402 fee is separate from the actual hotel charge taken by the property/Amadeus.

entries.name: NetIntel Calendar ICS Generator
entries.description: Turns structured event fields (title, start/end, timezone, location, etc.) into a valid RFC 5545 .ics calendar file with proper escaping, line folding, and a deterministic UID for idempotent re-import — so agents can publish events that import cleanly into Google, Apple, and Outlook calendars.

starts_at.description: ISO-8601 start. Use an offset/timestamp for timed events (e.g. 2026-06-27T09:00:00+02:00) or a bare date (YYYY-MM-DD) for all-day. Required.

ends_at.description: Optional ISO-8601 end. Defaults: timed -> start + 1 hour; all-day -> start + 1 day (exclusive). For multi-day all-day events pass the inclusive last day.

all_day.description: Optional. Inferred when omitted: a bare-date starts_at is all-day, a timestamp is timed.

timezone.description: Optional IANA timezone (e.g. Europe/Paris). Timed events are converted to UTC and emitted with a Z suffix (no VTIMEZONE block). Unrecognized values are ignored (falls back to UTC).

organizer.description: Optional organizer name and/or email -> ORGANIZER (CN=...).

ics.description: The full RFC 5545 .ics document (BEGIN:VCALENDAR ... END:VCALENDAR) with CRLF line endings

usage.callShape: POST https://netintel.dev/calendar/ics with Content-Type: application/json and a JSON body {title, starts_at, [ends_at], [all_day], [timezone], [location], [description], [url], [organizer]} (x402, USDC on Base eip155:8453 OR Solana; title and starts_at are the only required fields). Add ?download=1 or Accept: text/calendar to receive the raw .ics as a file attachment instead of the JSON envelope.
usage.outputShape: data{ics (full RFC 5545 VCALENDAR/VEVENT string with CRLF), uid (deterministic <hash>@netintel.dev), all_day}, score, grade, findings[]
quirks: Input is a JSON POST body (not query params); only title and starts_at are required.
Timed events are converted to UTC and emitted with a Z suffix and NO VTIMEZONE block (verified: starts_at 2026-06-27T09:00:00 + timezone Europe/Paris -> DTSTART:20260627T070000Z).
all_day is inferred from starts_at shape (bare date YYYY-MM-DD = all-day; timestamp = timed) unless explicitly set.
UID is deterministic (same inputs -> same UID) so re-importing the same event is idempotent across Google/Apple/Outlook.
Pure compute, no LLM. ?download=1 or Accept: text/calendar returns the raw .ics file with a Content-Disposition attachment header instead of the JSON envelope.
This host (netintel.dev) advertises TWO accepts: Base USDC (eip155:8453) AND Solana USDC — paid cleanly on Base at $0.005.
NetIntel does not charge on 4xx/5xx (input-validation, upstream, or server errors) per its agent fair-trade guarantee.
usage.guide: Turns event fields into a valid RFC 5545 .ics calendar file. POST https://netintel.dev/calendar/ics with Content-Type: application/json and a JSON body: title (required, SUMMARY) and starts_at (required, ISO-8601 timestamp for timed or bare YYYY-MM-DD for all-day). Optional: ends_at (defaults timed->+1h, all-day->+1 day exclusive; pass inclusive last day for multi-day), all_day (else inferred), timezone (IANA; timed events converted to UTC with a Z suffix, no VTIMEZONE), location, description, url, organizer. Pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base eip155:8453 or Solana). Returns data{ics, uid (deterministic, idempotent re-import), all_day}, score, grade, findings[]. Add ?download=1 (or Accept: text/calendar) to get the raw .ics file attachment instead of JSON. Use to publish agent-generated events that import cleanly into Google/Apple/Outlook calendars.

entries.name: NetIntel Holidays Check
entries.description: Looks up public holidays for any country and year (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), optionally checks whether a specific date is a holiday, weekend, or business day, and calculates the next business day — so agents can handle scheduling, SLA, and deadline logic without hardcoding country-specific holiday rules.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g. US, GB, DE) — required query param

year.description: 4-digit year (default: current year, range 2000-2099) — query param

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD specific date to check — populates date_check; omitted -> date_check is null — query param

usage.callShape: GET https://netintel.dev/holidays/check?country_code=<ISO2>[&year=<YYYY>][&date=<YYYY-MM-DD>] (x402, USDC on Base eip155:8453 OR Solana; no JSON body; country_code is a required query param, year and date optional)
usage.outputShape: country_code, year, total_holidays, holidays[]{date, name, local_name, is_global, types[]}, date_check{date, is_holiday, is_weekend, is_business_day, holiday_name, next_business_day} (null when no date passed), score, grade, findings[]
quirks: All inputs are QUERY PARAMS on a GET request (no JSON body): ?country_code=US&year=2026&date=2026-07-03
country_code is required; year defaults to the current year (range 2000-2099); date is optional — when omitted, date_check is null

date_check gives the actionable business-day answer: is_holiday, is_weekend, is_business_day, holiday_name, and next_business_day (verified: 2026-07-03 US -> Independence Day, next_business_day 2026-07-06)
This host (netintel.dev) advertises TWO accepts: Base USDC (eip155:8453) AND Solana USDC — paid cleanly on Base at $0.005
NetIntel does not charge on 4xx/5xx (input-validation, upstream, or server errors) per its agent fair-trade guarantee
holidays[] may contain duplicate dates with different type sets (e.g. Good Friday listed as both Public and Optional; Columbus Day as Public and Bank)
usage.guide: Looks up public holidays for a country/year and optionally answers date-aware scheduling questions (is a given date a holiday/weekend/business day, and what's the next business day). GET https://netintel.dev/holidays/check?country_code=<ISO2>[&year=<YYYY>][&date=<YYYY-MM-DD>] (x402, USDC on Base eip155:8453 OR Solana; no JSON body). country_code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) is required; year defaults to current year; date is optional. Output: country_code, year, total_holidays, holidays[]{date,name,local_name,is_global,types[]}, date_check{date,is_holiday,is_weekend,is_business_day,holiday_name,next_business_day} (null if no date given), score, grade, findings[]. Use for SLA/deadline math, scheduling, and date-aware workflows without hardcoding holiday rules.

entries.name: Greeneris Regional Holidays
entries.description: Subdivision-level public AND school holidays for ~36 mostly-European countries (German Laender, French academies, Spanish communities...), backed by the OpenHolidays API (data ODbL-1.0). Query by ISO country code and date window, optionally filtered to one ISO 3166-2 subdivision; each entry gives dates, English name, nationwide flag and the affected subdivision codes. Keyless over x402. $0.005.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, e.g. DE, FR, AT (required)

to.description: ISO end date (default: from + 6 months, max +366 days)

type.description: Holiday type: public holidays or school holidays

subdivision.description: Optional ISO 3166-2 subdivision filter, e.g. DE-BY

outputSchema.description: { ok, data: { country, holiday_type, from, to, subdivision, count, holidays: [ { start_date, end_date, name, type, nationwide, subdivisions: [string] } ], source } }

usage.callShape: GET /v1/eu/holidays-regional?country=<ISO2>&from=<YYYY-MM-DD>&to=<YYYY-MM-DD>&type=public|school&subdivision=<ISO 3166-2>
usage.outputShape: JSON: { ok:true, data:{ country, holiday_type, from, to, subdivision, count, holidays:[{ start_date, end_date, name, type, nationwide, subdivisions:[string] }], source } }
quirks: country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) is the only REQUIRED query param; from/to/type/subdivision are optional.
type=public returns public holidays (default); type=school returns school-holiday periods (which span multiple days: start_date != end_date).
Date window defaults to today + 6 months and is capped at 366 days.
nationwide:false holidays list the affected ISO 3166-2 subdivision codes in subdivisions[]; pass ?subdivision=DE-BY to filter to one region.
Verified: ?country=DE&from=2026-10-01&to=2026-11-05&type=public returned 3 holidays (Day of German Unity nationwide; Reformation Day and All Saints' Day regional).
Coverage is ~36 mostly-European countries via the OpenHolidays API (openholidaysapi.org); data ODbL-1.0, attribution required. 24h cache.
usage.guide: Regional/subdivision-level holiday calendar. Pass ?country= (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, required) plus optional from/to date window (default today +6mo, max 366 days), type=public|school (default public), and subdivision= (ISO 3166-2, e.g. DE-BY) to filter to one region. Read data.holidays[] for start_date, end_date, English name, nationwide flag and affected subdivisions[]. No API key; pay the x402 402 (Base USDC, $0.005).

entries.name: Greeneris French Business Days
entries.description: Adds N French business days to a start date, or counts business days over a range, skipping weekends and the 11 French legal public holidays (movable feasts via Butcher-Meeus) — so agents can compute French invoice/payment/SLA deadlines without hardcoding the holiday calendar.

start.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) to add business days to — use with add (add mode)

add.description: Business days to add, 1-366 (default 1) — use with start (add mode)

from.description: ISO range start (YYYY-MM-DD) — use with to (counting mode)

to.description: ISO range end (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive) — use with from (counting mode)

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/fr/business-days?start=<YYYY-MM-DD>&add=<1-366> (add mode) OR ?from=<YYYY-MM-DD>&to=<YYYY-MM-DD> (counting mode), optional &mode=ouvres|ouvrables (x402, USDC on Base eip155:8453; no JSON body — all inputs are query params)
usage.outputShape: { ok, data:{ mode, start, business_days_added, end_date, calendar_days, holidays_crossed[]{date,name}, source } } — in counting mode data reports the range and the business-day count instead of end_date
quirks: All inputs are QUERY PARAMS on a GET (no JSON body).

Two mutually-exclusive modes: ADD mode (start + add → end_date) vs COUNTING mode (from + to → business days in range). Verified add mode: start=2026-07-13 & add=30 → end_date 2026-08-25, crossing fete_nationale (07-14) and assomption (08-15).
mode=ouvres = Mon-Fri (default); mode=ouvrables = Mon-Sat.
Computed locally from French legal holidays (Code du travail L3133-1), Easter via Butcher-Meeus — deterministic, no external upstream.
Response is wrapped in { ok, data:{...} }; the 402/bazaar output example omits that wrapper but the live 200 includes it.
France-specific only — this is the /v1/fr/ dataset; sibling country paths (/v1/eu/holidays-regional, /v1/world/holidays) are separate services.
Host advertises only Base USDC (eip155:8453) in accepts — no Solana rail (unlike some sibling data hosts). Provider states buyers are never charged for empty or failed answers.
usage.guide: Computes French working-day deadlines. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/fr/business-days with query params (no JSON body), x402 USDC on Base. ADD mode: ?start=<YYYY-MM-DD>&add=<N 1-366> returns the date N French business days later. COUNTING mode: ?from=<YYYY-MM-DD>&to=<YYYY-MM-DD> counts business days in the inclusive range. Optional &mode=ouvres (Mon-Fri, default) or ouvrables (Mon-Sat). Skips weekends and the 11 French legal public holidays (movable feasts via Butcher-Meeus). Output: { ok, data:{ mode, start, business_days_added, end_date, calendar_days, holidays_crossed[]{date,name}, source } }. Use for French invoice/payment/SLA/legal deadline math without hardcoding the holiday calendar.

entries.name: Greeneris Space Launches
entries.description: Consolidated calendar of upcoming orbital launches worldwide (from Launch Library 2 by The Space Devs) with launch window (NET, window start/end), provider, pad and location, mission name/type/orbit, and go/TBD status, filterable by provider, free text and NET date range.

limit.description: Number of launches to return (1-25, query param, optional)

search.description: Free-text filter, e.g. falcon, starlink (query param, optional)

provider.description: Launch service provider name, e.g. SpaceX (query param, optional)

net_gte.description: Earliest NET, ISO date(-time) (query param, optional)

net_lte.description: Latest NET, ISO date(-time) (query param, optional)

usage.callShape: GET with optional query params: limit (integer 1-25, default 10), search (free text), provider (launch provider name), net_gte / net_lte (ISO date or date-time bounding the NET). All optional; a bare GET returns the next 10 upcoming launches. No body. Pure x402 pay-per-call on Base USDC; the 402 quote is the auth, no API key or account.
usage.outputShape: JSON object { ok: true, data: { total_upcoming, returned, launches: [{ id, name, provider, status, net, window_start, window_end, pad, location, mission, mission_type, orbit }], source } }. Verified 200 returned 5 upcoming Falcon launches (e.g. 'Falcon 9 Block 5 | Starlink Group 17-52', provider SpaceX, status Go, net 2026-08-01T02:00:00Z, pad Space Launch Complex 4E, Vandenberg SFB), with total_upcoming=127 for the falcon filter.
quirks: All parameters are optional query params (not path/body); a bare GET returns the next 10 launches. limit is capped at 25.
Result is wrapped in { ok, data } — the launches array lives under data.launches; data.total_upcoming is the full upcoming count matching the filter, data.returned is how many were included.
'orbit' can be null; 'status' is a human string (e.g. Go, TBD, Success). net is the No-Earlier-Than time; window_start/window_end bound the launch window.
Served from a 1h cache (upstream Launch Library 2 is rate-limited). Data source: Launch Library 2 by The Space Devs (thespacedevs.com).
Sibling ops on the same host (/v1/space/kp geomagnetic Kp index, /v1/solar/history) are separate services, not variants of this one.
usage.guide: Call GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/space/launches to get the upcoming orbital-launch calendar. Optionally narrow with limit (1-25), search (free text like 'falcon' or 'starlink'), provider (e.g. SpaceX), and net_gte / net_lte (ISO dates bounding the NET launch time). No body, no API key — pay $0.005 USDC on Base via x402. Read data.launches[] for each launch's name, provider, status, net (No-Earlier-Than time), window_start/window_end, pad, location and mission; data.total_upcoming gives the full upcoming count. Use for launch schedules, aerospace event calendars, and planning around upcoming missions.

entries.name: Greeneris Timezone Clock
entries.description: Current wall-clock time for any IANA timezone (ISO datetime, date, time, day of week and DST flag), resolved live against the IANA tz database.

tz.description: IANA timezone name (query param, required), e.g. Europe/Paris, America/New_York, Asia/Tokyo

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/time/zone?tz=Europe/Paris — single required query param tz (IANA timezone name). No body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key; the payment is the auth.
usage.outputShape: { ok: boolean, data: { timezone, datetime (ISO), date (YYYY-MM-DD), time (HH:MM:SS), day_of_week, dst_active: boolean, source } } — e.g. { ok: true, data: { timezone: 'Europe/Paris', datetime: '2026-07-30T19:42:43.9382711', date: '2026-07-30', time: '19:42:43', day_of_week: 'Thursday', dst_active: true, source: 'timeapi.io (IANA tz database)' } }
quirks: tz is a required query param (not path/body); it must be a valid IANA timezone name like Europe/Paris, America/New_York or Asia/Tokyo.
Result payload is wrapped in { ok, data } — the fields live under data.
Backed by timeapi.io / the IANA tz database (includes DST rules) and served with a ~60s cache — not a monotonic high-precision clock.
Sibling ops on the same host (e.g. /v1/world/holidays, /v1/eu/holidays-regional, /v1/fr/business-days) are separate services, not variants of this one.
usage.guide: Current wall-clock time for any IANA timezone. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/time/zone with a single required query param tz (IANA timezone name, e.g. Europe/Paris, America/New_York, Asia/Tokyo). No body, no API key — pay $0.001 USDC on Base via x402. Response: { ok: true, data: { timezone, datetime, date, time, day_of_week, dst_active, source } }. Data comes from the IANA tz database with DST rules and a ~60s cache. Use for scheduling, DST-aware timestamps and cross-timezone coordination.

entries.name: Greeneris World Holidays
entries.description: Returns the full list of official public holidays for one country and year (100+ countries, legally accurate dates from the Nager.Date registry), with English + local name, nationwide flag, regional counties and holiday types per entry.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, e.g. FR (required)

usage.callShape: GET with query params: country (required, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) and year (optional integer 1975-2077, defaults to current year). Pure x402 pay-per-call on Base USDC; the 402 quote is the auth, no API key or account.
usage.outputShape: JSON object { ok: true, data: { country, year, count, holidays: [{ date, local_name, name, nationwide, counties, types[] }], source } }. Verified 200 returned 11 French public holidays for 2026 (e.g. 2026-07-14 Bastille Day).
usage.quirks: Live 200 wraps the result in { ok, data: {...} } (the x402 402 outputSchema example omits the ok/data envelope and shows the fields flat — trust the live shape). 'counties' is null for nationwide holidays and lists regional codes for regional ones. Results cached 24h. Data sourced from the open-source MIT Nager.Date project (date.nager.at).
usage.guide: Pick a country by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g. FR, DE, US) and optionally a year (1975-2077; omit for current year). Call GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/world/holidays?country=FR&year=2026. Read data.holidays[] for each holiday's date, English name, local_name, nationwide flag, and types. Use for business-day/planning calculations and cross-border scheduling.

entries.name: 2s Business Days
entries.description: Holiday-aware business-day calculator for 200+ countries (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2): shift a date by N business days, count business days between two dates, or check whether a single date is a business day — skipping weekends and country/region holidays, with the skipped holidays itemized.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, e.g. US, DE, JP — required query param

start.description: Anchor date, YYYY-MM-DD — required query param

addDays.description: Signed integer number of business days to shift the start date by (e.g. 2, -3). XOR with end — provide exactly one of addDays or end; omit both to just check the start date

end.description: End date YYYY-MM-DD to count business days to (exclusive of start, inclusive of end). XOR with addDays

region.description: Optional subdivision code, e.g. CA (US-California), BY (DE-Bavaria) — query param

weekend.description: Optional comma-separated weekend days (default sat,sun; e.g. fri,sat for the Gulf) — query param

types.description: Optional comma-separated holiday types treated as closures (default public,bank) — query param

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/calendar/business-days?country=<ISO2>&start=<YYYY-MM-DD>[&addDays=<±N>|&end=<YYYY-MM-DD>][&region=<SUB>][&weekend=<csv>][&types=<csv>] (x402, USDC on Base eip155:8453 OR Solana; no JSON body; country and start are required query params)
usage.outputShape: data.ok (bool), data.total (int), data.items[]{mode ('add'|'between'|'check'), country, region, start, addDays, result (YYYY-MM-DD), calendarDaysSpanned (int), holidaysSkipped[]{date,name}}, data.source{provider,url,license}; plus top-level meta.cost.usd and meta.settlement{txHash,network,success}
quirks: All inputs are QUERY PARAMS on a GET request (no JSON body): ?country=US&start=2026-07-02&addDays=2
country and start are BOTH required

Three modes selected by which optional param you pass: start+addDays = shift by N business days (addDays is a SIGNED integer, negatives go backward); start+end = count business days between (exclusive of start, inclusive of end); start alone = check whether that one date is a business day
addDays XOR end — provide exactly one; passing both is ambiguous

Result payload is nested under data.* (data.items[], data.total, data.source); billing metadata is at top-level meta.cost.usd and meta.settlement — verified live response wraps under data.* even though the bazaar openapi example showed the fields at top level
Skipped weekend/holiday days that were stepped over are itemized in items[].holidaysSkipped[]{date,name} (e.g. 2026-07-03 'Independence Day (substitute day)')

Optional weekend overrides the default sat,sun (e.g. weekend=fri,sat for Gulf countries); optional types overrides which holiday types count as closures (default public,bank); optional region narrows to a subdivision (e.g. region=CA)
Data source is the date-holidays rule set computed locally by 2s.io (ISC code + CC BY 3.0 holiday data) — attribute date-holidays / CC BY 3.0
Advertises two accepts: Base USDC (eip155:8453) and Solana USDC; paid cleanly on Base at $0.001
usage.guide: Compute business days across weekends and country/region holidays. GET https://2s.io/api/calendar/business-days with required query params country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, 200+ supported) and start (YYYY-MM-DD). Pick one of three modes: add addDays=<signed integer> to shift start by N business days (negatives go backward); add end=<YYYY-MM-DD> to count business days from start (exclusive) to end (inclusive); or pass neither to check whether start itself is a business day. addDays and end are mutually exclusive. Optionally add region=<subdivision> (e.g. CA for US-California), weekend=<comma-separated days> to override the default sat,sun (e.g. fri,sat for the Gulf), and types=<comma-separated> to change which holiday types count as closures (default public,bank). No request body. Pay per call via x402 ($0.001 USDC on Base eip155:8453, also settleable in Solana USDC); no API key. Result is synchronous JSON nested under data.*: read data.items[0].result for the computed date, data.items[0].calendarDaysSpanned for elapsed calendar days, and data.items[0].holidaysSkipped[] for the weekend/holiday days stepped over. Use for payment terms, SLA/deadline math, and delivery-date estimates. Verified 2026-07-30 with addDays=2&country=US&start=2026-07-02 -> HTTP 200, result 2026-07-07 (skipped 2026-07-03 Independence Day substitute day), $0.001 charged (tx 0x611394ec1885438142c9ba2c5cf597d550bada51e2a17a6969f621fea39ff4d5).

entries.name: 2s Holidays
entries.description: Lists the official holidays for a country and year (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, 200+ countries) with exact observed dates including substitute days, optionally filtered by region subdivision, holiday type, and localized language — computed from maintained per-country rules (movable feasts + lunar-calendar holidays).

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, e.g. US, DE, JP — required query param

year.description: Calendar year, e.g. 2026 — required query param

region.description: Optional subdivision code, e.g. CA (US-California), BY (DE-Bavaria) — query param

types.description: Optional comma-separated filter: public, bank, school, optional, observance — query param

lang.description: Optional ISO 639-1 language for localized holiday names — query param

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/calendar/holidays?country=<ISO2>&year=<YYYY>[&region=<SUB>][&types=<csv>][&lang=<ISO639-1>] (x402, USDC on Base eip155:8453 OR Solana; no JSON body; country and year are required query params)
usage.outputShape: data.ok (bool), data.total (int), data.items[]{date (YYYY-MM-DD), name, type, substitute (bool), rule}, data.source{provider,url,license}, data.meta{country,region,year}; plus top-level meta.cost.usd and meta.settlement{txHash,network,success}
quirks: All inputs are QUERY PARAMS on a GET request (no JSON body): ?country=US&year=2026&types=public
country and year are BOTH required (unlike NetIntel's holidays check where year defaults) — omitting year still returns but pin it explicitly
Result payload is nested under data.* (data.items[], data.total, data.source, data.meta); billing metadata is at top-level meta.cost.usd and meta.settlement
substitute:true rows mark observed/substitute days (e.g. 2026-07-03 'Independence Day (substitute day)' alongside the real 2026-07-04) — expect duplicate-name pairs around weekend holidays
Each item carries a human-readable rule string (e.g. '3rd monday in January') showing how the date is computed
Optional region narrows to a subdivision (e.g. region=CA for US-California, region=BY for DE-Bavaria); optional types filters public|bank|school|optional|observance; optional lang localizes names
Data source is the date-holidays rule set computed locally by 2s.io (ISC code + CC BY 3.0 holiday data) — attribute date-holidays / CC BY 3.0
Advertises two accepts: Base USDC (eip155:8453) and Solana USDC; paid cleanly on Base at $0.001
usage.guide: List a country's official holidays for a year with exact observed dates. GET https://2s.io/api/calendar/holidays?country=<ISO2>&year=<YYYY> — country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, 200+ supported) and year are required query params; optionally add region=<subdivision> (e.g. CA for US-California, BY for DE-Bavaria), types=<comma-separated: public,bank,school,optional,observance>, and lang=<ISO 639-1> for localized names. No request body. Pay per call via x402 ($0.001 USDC on Base eip155:8453, also settleable in Solana USDC); no API key. Result is synchronous JSON: read holidays from data.items[] — each is {date (YYYY-MM-DD), name, type, substitute, rule}, with data.total and data.source (date-holidays / CC BY 3.0). Substitute/observed days appear as separate substitute:true rows. Use for scheduling, delivery estimates, payment terms, and SLA/deadline math. Verified 2026-07-31 with country=US&types=public&year=2026 -> HTTP 200, 12 holidays, $0.001 charged (tx 0x0c5df4707fc0fd20c95f7bd53d7d1f1ca0830c25c37c6d5b44eb7936cc3e65dc).

entries.name: Strale Holiday Calendar
entries.description: Public holidays for a given country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) and year across 100+ countries, with holiday names, dates, types (Public/Bank/Optional/Observance/School), local names, and whether they are global or region-specific.

year.description: Year (optional; defaults to the current year)

usage.callShape: GET https://api.strale.io/x402/holiday-calendar?country_code=US&year=2026 (query params: country_code = required ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code; year = optional integer, defaults to current year); x402 USDC on Base
usage.outputShape: { country_code, year, total_holidays (int), holidays: [{ date (YYYY-MM-DD), name, local_name, type ('Public'|'Bank'|'Optional'|'Observance'|'School'), fixed (bool), global (bool), counties (array of ISO subdivision codes like 'US-CA', or null when global) }] }; provenance/payment under body._meta (capability, latency_ms, provenance.source='nager.date', payment.settlement_id/price_usd). Verified: country_code=US year=2026 -> total_holidays 17 (New Year's Day, MLK Day, Presidents Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas, etc.).
quirks: `country_code` is required (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2); `year` is optional and defaults to the current year.
A holiday can appear multiple times for one date with different `type`/`counties` (e.g. 2026 Columbus Day is returned as both a state-level 'Public' entry and a nationwide 'Bank' entry).
`counties` lists ISO 3166-2 subdivision codes when the holiday is region-specific (global=false); it is null for nationwide holidays.
Underlying data is from nager.date (see body._meta.provenance.source); provenance and settlement metadata are returned under body._meta.
Strale exposes a near-duplicate /x402/public-holiday-lookup op on the same host (also nager.date) at a different price/output shape; this service is the /x402/holiday-calendar path.
usage.guide: Get public holidays for a country and year. Make a GET request to https://api.strale.io/x402/holiday-calendar with the required query param country_code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. US) and an optional year (integer, defaults to the current year), e.g. ?country_code=US&year=2026. Pay the fixed $0.0216 x402 quote (USDC on Base, no API key) and retry with the payment header. The 200 returns plain JSON: read body.total_holidays for the count and iterate body.holidays[] for each holiday's date, name, local_name, type, and (for region-specific ones) counties. Payment/provenance are under body._meta.
